description: Use fluctuation-stabilized and noise-dependent memories as a search strategy rather than as a claim about the proof system itself. Carefully injected stochasticity may help the search escape brittle local motifs before a deterministic extraction stage decides whether anything exact and useful was found.
mathematical_formalization: Let \rho_\eta be a stochastic local rule with noise parameter \eta. Define F(\eta)=\mathbb{E}[S_{\mathrm{extract}}(\rho_\eta)] and run an annealed search over \eta and rule parameters, keeping only motifs whose deterministic compiled core remains legal when \eta\to 0 or after freezing the discovered pattern.
analogical_connections: Noise acts as a catalyst for motif discovery, not as part of the final proof.
Fluctuation-stabilized order is analogous to a search process that needs randomness to reveal hidden low-score basins.
Annealing over CA noise mirrors simulated annealing over combinatorial certificate space.
implementation_hypothesis: Start from promising discrete rules and add controlled asynchronous noise, site dropout, or tie-breaking randomness during search only. Once a good motif is found, freeze the discovered local structure and rerun exact deterministic extraction to see if the benefit survives.
experiment_seed: Compare noise-free, fixed-noise, and annealed-noise searches on the same rule family and extraction backend. Track whether stochastic search improves the best exact score or just produces non-reproducible motifs.

novelty_claim: The novelty is methodological: use stochastic memory phenomena to improve exploration of exact certificate space, then strip the noise away before claiming success.
differentiation: This is not a stochastic proof system. If exact deterministic extraction does not preserve the gain, the concept fails by design.
